title: Flexible Intensities Matter: A Comprehensive Re-evaluation of Hawkes Processes and Neural Temporal Point Processes
abstract: arXiv:2611.06348v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Temporal point processes (TPPs) are the canonical framework for event sequence data, with applications spanning seismology, social media, and electronic health records. Recently, neural TPPs have been reported to substantially outperform classical TPPs, such as Hawkes processes, but these comparisons pitted flexible neural models against Hawkes processes in their most restricted form, and did not consider large-scale medical data. Here, we revisit this comparison through a systematic evaluation of Poisson and Hawkes processes of increasing flexibility against neural TPPs, on five established benchmark datasets and on two large-scale medical evaluation tasks derived from UK Biobank disease histories and MIMIC-IV ICU records, under autoregressive next-event prediction. translated_title: 柔性强度至关重要：对霍克斯过程与神经时间点过程的全面重新评估
translated_abstract: 时间点过程（TPPs）是事件序列数据的标准框架，其应用涵盖地震学、社交媒体和电子健康记录等领域。最近有报道称神经TPPs大幅优于经典TPPs（如霍克斯过程），但这些比较是将灵活的神经模型与形式最受限制的霍克斯过程进行对比，且未涉及大规模医疗数据。在此，我们通过系统性评估重新审视了这一比较：在五个成熟的基准数据集以及两个分别源自英国生物银行（UK Biobank）疾病史和MIMIC-IV重症监护记录的大规模医疗评估任务上，在自回归下一事件预测设置下，对灵活性逐步提升的泊松过程和霍克斯过程与神经TPPs进行了对比。首先，一旦为霍克斯过程配备灵活可学习的基线和核函（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过对标准基准和大规模医疗数据的系统性重新评估发现，一旦为霍克斯过程配备灵活可学习的基线与核函数，其与神经时间点过程之间此前报道的性能差距基本消失，从而挑战了神经TPPs显著优于经典TPPs的结论。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically re-evaluates Hawkes processes against neural temporal point processes on established benchmarks and large-scale medical datasets, showing that the previously reported performance gap largely disappears once Hawkes processes are equipped with flexible, learnable baselines and kernels.
